bias: Financial conditions look little-changed since early July on the surface, but the composition has shifted: the RRP buffer is effectively drained and TGA has resumed building, while the yield curve has bear-steepened (30Y +12.5bps, 10Y +8.7bps) even as credit and vol stay calm. counterargs.read: The tape looks calm — vol is low, credit is tight, semis are leading — but the plumbing underneath has quietly worsened: the RRP cushion that absorbed prior QT/TGA swings is now nearly gone, and the long end of the curve is repricing higher without a matching front-end move. That combination (calm risk assets + draining liquidity buffer + rising term premium) is the setup to watch into the Aug 27 H.4.1 print and the Sept 15-16 FOMC, not an active warning yet.

duration_score.reason: 10Y and 30Y yields both rose since Jul (10Y +8.7bps, 30Y +12.5bps) while the front end (2Y, 3M) stayed flat-to-down — a bear-steepening driven by long-end term premium, not front-end Fed expectations. Credit remains calm (HY OAS flat, COF firm) and breakevens have only ticked up modestly (+4 to +7bps), so this doesn't read as acute inflation panic, but it argues against adding long duration ahead of the Sept 15-16 FOMC.

james_framework.what_market_IS_saying: Front-end (2Y, 3M) pricing is stable/sticky while the long end sells off — the market is repricing term premium/fiscal supply, not near-term Fed policy.
james_framework.pain_trade: Long-duration holders (TLT) — steepening hurts long bonds even as the front end stays anchored.
james_framework.watch_signal: If 2Y starts falling while 30Y keeps rising, that's classic bull-steepening/cuts being priced in. That is NOT currently happening — 2Y is flat, not falling.
